description: Production Turbopack gzip baselines for every canonical preview route after the examples were made self-contained. The checker requires exact coverage of exampleSlugs, allows the larger of 2% or 5 KiB growth per example and 5 KiB for the shared host, rejects stale builds and shared route-owned chunks, and supplements those checks with surviving WGSL source markers. ML runtimes and model files are fetched dynamically as public assets and are not attributed to route chunks.
$comment:tgeist-08: Twenty previously over-limit routes were remeasured from one Node 22 / Next 16.3.3 production build after integration of strict binding checks and the updated canary library/toolchain: gradient through air-painting, excluding optimized-black-hole and glass-fractal. The other eight route baselines and shared host retain their earlier Node 22 / Next 16.3.2 measurements. Shared library growth is intentional; this measurement does not isolate the toolchain's byte contribution or claim two-build confirmation. Growth allowances and structural checks are unchanged. previousAppsDocsBaseline remains read-only historical provenance, including examples that no longer exist.
$comment:three-tsl: three-tsl is the outlier here at ~279 KB against a 15-85 KB field, and deliberately so: it is the advanced three.js integration example, so three.js core, the TSL node system, WebGPURenderer and BloomNode are the subject of the example rather than incidental weight. Adding the second Three route made Turbopack factor 238179 B gzip of shared Three code into its own chunk; a same-build control with the former local helper measured 276833 B, so vgpu/three itself adds only 2280 B to this route. The HDRI it lights with is served from public/examples/three-tsl/sunset.exr instead of the inlined @pmndrs/assets data URI, which keeps ~147 KB of base64 out of this number. Treat a regression against this baseline the same as any other; do not treat the baseline itself as a precedent for non-three examples.
$comment:tsl-exports: The focused tslExports route is 239570 B gzip: a 238179 B shared Three/TSL/WebGPURenderer chunk plus 1391 B of route-owned example code. Renaming the route shortened both the adapter and former-local-helper builds by 4 B, so the same-build control remains a 2285 B adapter delta. Keep this route intentionally small even though the framework it demonstrates dominates its transfer size.
$comment:glass-sculpture: Measured at 72804 B gzip from the current canary production build on Node 22.21.1; the external proposal's provisional 78000 B value was not carried forward. Remeasured with the other #484 integration routes below.
$comment:matcap: Measured at 70640 B gzip from the current canary production build on Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3 after the reviewed lifecycle and vertex-shading refinements.
$comment:video-to-texture: Measured at 68829 B gzip from the current canary production build on Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3 after lifecycle, media-provenance, and current texture-API integration.
$comment:draw-retention-integration: Thirteen routes were remeasured with `node scripts/check-example-bundles.mjs --update=instanced-rendering,batch-rendering,typegpu-liquid-glass,adaptive-quality,atmosphere,glass-sculpture,spiral-galaxy,liquid-layout,spring-choreography,kinetic-sculpture,modular-city,marble-machine,mechanical-garden` from one Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3 production build (local macOS) of the merge of draw-consumer lifetimes (#484) with the managed uniform reuse canary (#483): those routes exceeded baseline plus allowed growth, while every other route stayed within its existing baseline and is unchanged. The likely contributor is shared vgpu runtime growth (the root client entry measures 51475 B gzip against the 47616 B canary budget); the measurement does not isolate runtime from toolchain bytes for baselines recorded before Next 16.3.3. Growth allowances and isolation checks are unchanged.

previousAppsDocsBaseline.$comment: Read-only provenance, not used by check-example-bundles.mjs: the numbers this file carried in apps/docs, so the before/after table can be regenerated from the repo alone. apps/docs keeps its own copy of this file, unmodified, until cutover (TGEIST-15).

$comment:spiral-galaxy: Measured at 86662 B gzip on Node 22.21.1 against canary c290dd32, with batched compute/render submission, compute prewarming, unchanged shader output, and a static vgpu import inside the lazy-loaded example.
$comment:spiral-galaxy-shared-chunks: Adding Spiral Galaxy changes Turbopack chunk factoring: an isolated clean-canary control at 7d51e9db measures Atmosphere at 111457 B gzip, versus 111604 B with this example, using the same Node 22.21.1 and lockfile. Increase only Atmosphere's baseline by the measured 147 B delta (106391 to 106538), preserving its existing 54 B remaining allowance; its source and all growth rules remain unchanged. The updated c290dd32 candidate reproduces the same 111604 B measurement.
$comment:scene-composition: Ten camera-migrated examples were remeasured by the checker from the final scene-composition production build on Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3. Atmosphere was also remeasured: an unchanged-app control build already exceeded its old ceiling, and the feature build is 168 bytes smaller than that control. Growth allowances, shared-host budget, isolation/freshness checks, other routes and historical provenance are unchanged.
$comment:liquid-layout: Measured at 139352 B gzip from a production build of this branch (canary cdf24a18 plus Liquid Layout and Spring Choreography) on Node 24.13.0 / Next 16.3.3. Motion's React layout/drag/presence layer dominates: the 23010 B React Motion chunk plus the 24697 B Motion core chunk it shares with Spring Choreography. The route-owned code and WGSL measure 25182 B (WGSL ships with its comments); the rest is the two chunks every route loads (49880 B, including the vgpu runtime) and the 16583 B lil-gui/vgpu chunk shared with Glass Sculpture, Spiral Galaxy and Spring Choreography.
$comment:liquid-layout-shared-chunks: Adding Liquid Layout changes Turbopack chunk factoring: Spiral Galaxy's raw bytes stay at 272348 B, but its lil-gui code moves into the lil-gui/vgpu chunk that Glass Sculpture already loads, now shared by all three lil-gui routes. A same-machine control of the same tree with this example removed measures Spiral Galaxy at 86777 B gzip, versus 87311 B with it, on the same Node 22.21.1 and lockfile. Increase only Spiral Galaxy's baseline by the measured 534 B delta (86662 to 87196); its source and all growth rules remain unchanged. Atmosphere measures the same 111816 B in both local builds, so this example does not move it (canary CI run 36044722520 measures it at 111628 B).
$comment:spring-choreography: Measured at 116092 B gzip from a production build of this branch (canary cdf24a18 plus Liquid Layout and this example) on Node 24.13.0 / Next 16.3.3. The route loads no React Motion: vanilla Motion's core (animate, spring, stagger, frame) is a 24697 B chunk shared with Liquid Layout, and springValue with the vgpu compute runtime adds 3471 B. The example code and six WGSL modules are 21461 B; the rest is the two chunks every route loads (49880 B, including the vgpu runtime) and the 16583 B lil-gui/vgpu chunk shared with Glass Sculpture, Spiral Galaxy and Liquid Layout.
$comment:spring-choreography-shared-chun: Adding Spring Choreography does not move any non-Motion route: Glass Sculpture matches canary CI run 36044722520 exactly (73289 B), Spiral Galaxy still measures 87311 B, and Atmosphere still reads the same 111816 B here (111628 B in that CI run).
$comment:scene-gallery: Measured together from the final three-example production build on Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3: Kinetic Sculpture 98611 B, Modular City 108272 B, Marble Machine 133147 B gzip. These include the shared runtime chunks; Marble Machine also includes the docs-only cannon-es physics dependency. The checker passed isolation and existing route limits before these three measured entries were added. All 35 existing example baselines, the shared-host budget, growth allowances and historical provenance are unchanged.
$comment:mechanical-garden: Measured at 142492 B gzip from the robot-training-ground production build on Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3. The route-owned chunk is 53023 B, including the quadruped geometry, exclusive DOM toolbar, seven WGSL modules and selected math utilities; the remaining 89469 B are shared runtime chunks, including vgpu/scene and lil-gui. All 38 other routes pass their unchanged budgets; the shared-host budget, growth allowances and isolation checks are unchanged. math remains a private docs-app dependency.
$comment:device-loss: Only holographic-card was remeasured by the official checker after gpu.lost: a fresh Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3 production build measured 75367 B gzip, identical to Linux CI, versus 75070 B on exact-base canary 8c048592. Its previous baseline was 69978 B, leaving only 28 B before this feature. The 297 B shared-runtime growth is intentional; the remaining 38 routes pass their existing limits. Shared-host baseline, growth allowances, chunk isolation/freshness rules and historical provenance are unchanged.
$comment:surface-depth-msaa: Only triangle-led-front, fluid, depth-estimation and air-painting were remeasured by the official checker from a fresh Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3 production build after opt-in Surface depth/MSAA. Against exact-base canary 86d1f01b CI, their shared-runtime growth is 697, 715, 647 and 647 gzip bytes respectively; all four crossed their remaining allowance. The other 35 route baselines (including holographic-card), shared-host baseline, growth allowances, isolation/freshness rules and historical provenance are unchanged.
$comment:managed-uniform-reuse: Only gradient, anti-aliasing, black-hole, earth, fft-ocean, fft-ocean-surface, raymarched-fractal, glass-fractal, environment-map, clipping, matcap, video-to-texture, radiance-cascades, agent-radiance-cascades, nextjs-flare, mnist-classifier and transmission were remeasured by the official checker (--update) from a fresh Node 22.21.1 / Next 16.3.3 production build after issue 483 (bind-group cache index, pooled frame uniform pages, packed-byte equality, raw buffer ranges). Against exact-base canary c5ab0e8f CI, the shared runtime grew about 0.86-0.93 KB gzip per route (gradient 59583 -> 60444 B, anti-aliasing 74652 -> 75517 B, transmission 92812 -> 93739 B at the final build; local gradient matched the CI-plus-delta estimate within 1 B), which pushed these routes, already within about 0.9 KB of their limits, over the 5 KiB allowance. Other routes and the shared host keep their earlier baselines; growth allowances and structural checks are unchanged.
